clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991, within the year: you hurt your wrist in your first term at the conservatory in October, lost your footing and fell into anxiety and low functioning; you and Rafe clashed in November and he moved out; you were holed up getting high and absorbed in radios by late autumn; and by early 1992 you were lost and low, unable to get going, with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry. Your father's shift toward his own father in early 1989 sits outside these months.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother's diagnosis in 2001 or 2002, within the two years: you were running out of steam for performing by September 2001, anxious and low in functioning; you had a disastrous audition in early 2002 and were done with performing; you were on poor terms with family and friends by September 2002; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour that same month; you met Marisol in January 2003 and moved to Fenwick with her in June; you split from her by October and sank into deep depression once back in Thornbury that winter; you could not face your family, anxious and distant; you relied gingerly on friends Corbin, Dale and Silas instead; and you cut off from your mother when you left for nursing school in August 2008, the silence holding for roughly a year. Your grandmother spent her final months in your mother's home in the autumn of 2003 and died in February 2004.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2019
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within the decade: you were too drained for conversation with your mother at Alder Creek in July 2008; she pressed to visit you, you were anxious and told her repeatedly the timing was wrong, and you kept the door shut on her; you cut off from her entirely when you left for nursing school that August. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation. A decade later, in October 2019, your partner Wren was swamped with a street party, a fundraising dinner, and the drive to the lake for her mother's retirement party; you were too strict laying out a plan to settle her when she was swamped, anxious and overfunctioning; she talks with her father and brother all day, nothing happening to one that the others don't hear; you were awake from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep, symptom and anxiety up, distant from the family, feeling you don't belong; and Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. Your aunt Imogen's memory loss and conflict with her son Hal began around 2015 and 2018. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017. These shifts nest in a long quiet from your grandmother's death until your partner came along.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
